tasks.short: Collaborate on computer-science teaching and research issues.

steps.what: Examine relevant teaching examples or research code before discussion
Discuss teaching or research issues and agree joint technical actions
Write agreed actions with links to the relevant technical artefacts
Verify final action wording and artefact version references
Save the approved technical collaboration note

tasks.design: Use a native action-note layout in {DOCS} with reusable references to the course or research artefacts under discussion. The lecturer still examines the material, discusses the issue and writes actual agreed actions; the template removes repeated headings and reference descriptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Action notes repeat technical artefact names and meeting scaffolding.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and note templates can reuse verified references.
tasks.still_hard: Research disagreements and teaching choices need substantive discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Understand a colleague's reasoning and agree a defensible joint action.
tasks.altitude: A small note-assembly reduction; collaboration and decision rights stay unchanged.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for document access and national consultation if applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reusable action-note references reduce repeated scaffolding without resolving teaching or research issues.

assumptions: Boundary: focal lecturer preparation, joint discussion and existing technical action notes. Colleague participation and software/research implementation are unchanged, outside focal savings.

Existing course/research owners supply artefact_id, version and location. s2 produces actual agreed actions; s3 captures action_text, owner, due_date and reference manually. Missing references retain manual writing; no transcript or decision feed is assumed.
Test native document templates first. s5 is a near-zero native save, minimum 1% fully retained. Shares are provisional work estimates independent of prompt priors.
Gross saving 4.2%; focal upkeep 0.5 gives net 3.7%.
research_questions: Does a linked note retain the precise artefact version discussed?

already_counted.description: Verify agreed technical actions and references

approvals.approved_version: approved technical note v1 final action text and artefact versions; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% for already-linked notes with no deployment; 3% if stale references cost 0.7 extra baseline hours versus central net 3.7%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and obtain textbooks and laboratory supplies.

steps.what: Define teaching requirements for textbooks or laboratory equipment
Search approved textbook and laboratory equipment catalogues
Evaluate pedagogic fit, technical compatibility and price
Complete the purchase requisition for selected resources
Verify final quantities, specifications and requisition destination
Submit the approved requisition to purchasing
Receive resources and inspect delivered items against the request
Enter and verify actual receipt details
Save the verified resource receipt

tasks.design: Configure approved catalogue filters and catalogue-to-requisition field reuse in {PROCUREMENT}, using the library catalogue category of {OTHER} where applicable. The lecturer evaluates teaching and technical fit, verifies the request and later records the actual inspected receipt; purchasing and supplier delivery remain their existing work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogue selection can be followed by repeated specification entry into requisitions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue links and field transfer avoid retyping known item details.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching suitability, equipment compatibility and substitutions need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose resources that fit actual course activities and laboratory constraints.
tasks.altitude: Less catalogue navigation and requisition entry; procurement authority does not change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-8 for catalogue and budget access plus applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked catalogue items can populate requisition fields while pedagogic selection and physical receipt stay human.

assumptions: Boundary: lecturer selection, requisition and receipt. Purchasing approval/order and supplier delivery are unchanged outside the focal denominator, with no new transfer to those roles.

Existing catalogue owners supply item_id, edition_or_specification, supplier, price and unit. s1 defines needs; s4 captures quantity and budget_code. s7 observes actual delivery; s8 records received_quantity and discrepancy. Missing catalogue fields retain manual entry.
Test native catalogue/requisition settings first. s6/s9 are near-zero native commits at minimum 1% each fully retained. No planned order quantity is treated as actual receipt.
Gross saving 13.5%; focal catalogue-link upkeep 1 gives central net 12.5%.
unknowns: Who records the delivery receipt today
research_questions: Does field reuse preserve textbook edition and equipment specification exactly?

approvals.approved_version: approved resource requisition v1 final items, quantities and budget code; edits void approval
approved resource receipt v1 actual inspected delivery details; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% if catalogues already populate requests and no change is made; 10% if unmatched items retain 2.5 more baseline hours than central net 12.5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Serve on academic and administrative committees.

steps.what: Read committee papers on policy, departmental or academic matters
Prepare and verify written comments or proposed amendments
Submit the approved comments to the committee document space
Deliberate with committee members and challenge proposed decisions
Take a position and vote within the committee mandate

tasks.design: Use the existing committee template in {DOCS} to carry agenda references and amendment headings into written comments. Reading, deliberation and voting retain all their time; the lecturer writes and verifies each substantive comment before submitting it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Written contributions repeatedly restate agenda and document references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can reuse those references.
tasks.still_hard: Policy trade-offs and institutional responsibilities cannot be delegated to a template.
tasks.human_edge: Represent academic concerns and take responsibility for a committee position.
tasks.altitude: A small comment-formatting saving; voting rights remain unchanged.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for committee access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: committee contribution templates can reduce repeated reference headings without drafting substantive positions.

assumptions: Boundary: member preparation, existing written comments, meeting and position-taking. Official minutes are the secretary's unchanged work and are not folded into participation or claimed as saving.

Committee secretariat supplies agenda_item_id, paper_version and document_reference. s2 manually authors comments and verifies their meaning; the template supplies headings only. Missing references retain manual preparation.
Test native templates first. s3 is near-zero native submission at minimum 1%, fully retained. Gross 3%; focal upkeep 0.3 gives net 2.7%.
unknowns: Whether members submit written comments today
research_questions: Does a template preserve a clear link to the exact paper version?

already_counted.description: Author and verify substantive committee comments

approvals.approved_version: approved committee comments v1 final comments and paper references; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% if comments already use the template and no change is made; 2% when upkeep takes one rather than central 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events.

steps.what: Join campus events and community computing activities in person

tasks.design: Keep the lecturer's personal participation in campus and community computing events. An existing {CALENDAR} entry can show the event program, but does not replace the contribution or shorten attendance.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change shortens that output.
tasks.still_hard: Useful engagement depends on the audience and local relationships.
tasks.human_edge: Connect academic computing with the people attending.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the lecturer's week or decision rights.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: event participation has no inherent administrative artefact or digital substitute.

assumptions: Boundary is participation, not event organisation, registration, promotional writing or a required report. No record, lookup or send is hidden in the in-person step; check any institution-specific paperwork separately.
Inputs are an existing program and invitation. No structured data or new capture is needed. Native calendar configuration was considered and provides no attendance-time saving.
Zero upkeep because no new tool, process or labour transfer is introduced.
unknowns: Whether a local event contribution includes a separate required written deliverable
research_questions: Does observation reveal genuine event paperwork beyond participation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Personal participation remains unchanged; no unstated event-administration baseline is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated reference and requisition work while preserving teaching and research discussion, committee judgement and community presence.
reach: Help laboratory coordinators specify teaching resources
role.ambitious_version: A computer science lecturer with clear technical action records and reliable teaching resources who retains time for colleagues and the community.
